messages:
incidents-bot: Paging: error-rate spike detected on `reranker-service` -> /internal/batch-embed endpoint. 5xx rate > 8% over last 3m. Severity: SEV2. @maya (oncall) you're up. :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): saw the page. Looking at logs now. Is this affecting hosted customers or just internal jobs?

Sam (support): customer support flagged two large customers seeing failed search re-ranks and slow tail latencies. Tickets #5462 and #5463 opened. Both report ~20% of queries returning "vector mismatch" errors.

maya (oncall): copying logs from the batch processor. Paste a short excerpt: ```2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR batch-serializer: InvalidVectorLength: expected=768 got=512 request_id=abc123 worker=be-07```

Jae L: that InvalidVectorLength matches the reranker client's assertion. We changed default model in staging last week from rw-bert-768 to rw-lite-512 — could be a model/compat mismatch sneaking into production.

Priya R: timeline: 13:50 deploy of embedder pipeline v2.3.1 to canary (automated). 13:54 canary promoted to 30% routing. 14:00 full rollout to prod. Errors start ~14:02.

maya (oncall): Hypothesis 1: rollout pushed a 512-dim encoder into the batcher that still advertises 768 to reranker. Hypothesis 2: serde change in batch composer dropped a trailing chunk for some batched payloads (partial truncate). Hypothesis 3: downstream reranker backward compat check started rejecting shorter vectors due to stricter validation.

Theo (infra): pulling node-level metrics. Not seeing GPU OOMs. CPU on the batch composer spiked at 14:01 but recovered. Network looks fine.

maya (oncall): mitigation options: 1) rollback embedder v2.3.1 to pinned v2.3.0 (fast), 2) temporarily disable batching on /internal/batch-embed for 1h, 3) add a compatibility shim in reranker to accept 512 and upsample to 768 (risky). Thoughts?

Jae L: can we flip traffic back to v2.3.0 canary? The rollout is recent; rollback should be quick and safe. I can do it if we agree.

Priya R: signal from support: customers want mitigation asap, rollback preferred. They'd prefer fewer false positives than a degraded throughput.

maya (oncall): I'm going to run a controlled rollback to v2.3.0 on one region and observe. Marking the thread for a 15m check-in.

SRE-Bot: action logged: rollback start by maya (oncall) at 2026-03-15T14:10:02Z -> target service: embedder-pool-prod -> version: v2.3.0

maya (oncall): rollback complete on us-west-2 at 14:16. Error rate dropped to ~0.7% within 2 minutes. Pushing rollback to all regions now.

Sam (support): notifying affected customers that we're rolling back and investigating root cause. Sending a short status update message now.

Priya R: collecting artifact: can we get the exact failing payload that triggered InvalidVectorLength? Jae, earliest request_id abc123 from logs — is there a trace?

Jae L: got the full request payload cached by the batch handler. Sharing sanitized excerpt: ```{"batch_size":10, "vectors":[{"len":768},{"len":768},...,{"len":512},...]}``` shows one vector at position 7 with length 512. The batch assembler logged `serialized_bytes=6144` but expected 9216 for 12 vectors x 768.

maya (oncall): interesting. So the batch assembler sometimes emits mixed-dimension batches. That explains why reranker throws on validation. Where would mixed dims originate? Either upstream model changed or a bug in the aggregator that merges outputs from multiple shards.

Theo (infra): checking model-serving logs for the embedder instances deployed in the rollout. 13:57-14:02 there's a mixed fleet: some instances running v2.3.0 serving 768d, some v2.3.1 serving 512d — rollout did not fully drain older pods before starting new ones in the canary -> full rollout path. Race condition in the deployment pipeline.

Priya R: root cause theory w/ evidence: deployment orchestration allowed overlap of differing model variants during the rollout window; batch composer isn't dimension-safe and will assemble outputs from any replica it hits. When a single 512d vector joins a 768d batch, downstream validation fails with InvalidVectorLength.

maya (oncall): mitigation validated: full rollback to v2.3.0 across regions reduced customer errors. Next steps: block immediate re-rollout, patch deployment pipeline to avoid mixed-variant overlap, and add batch-level sanity checks (reject mixed-dim batches or pad/upsample as last resort).

Jae L: I'll open a PR for batch assembler to validate vector dimensionality before forming a batch and add metrics for "mixed-dim batches". Will include a small upsample shim for emergency use.

Theo (infra): will add a gating step to the deployment job to ensure zero-instance overlap when model-dimensionality changes are detected. Also adding a preflight that compares model metadata (dim, dtype) across the fleet; fail the rollout if mismatch.

Sam (support): I'll send updated customer comms: incident mitigated, rollback applied, engineering investigating RCA and ETA for fix.

maya (oncall): logging action items here: * rollback performed (maya) * collect all request_ids with InvalidVectorLength (Jae) * PR for batch validation + emergency shim (Jae) * deployment gating change (Theo) * customer comms + incident timeline (Sam) * postmortem doc (Priya)

Priya R: adding preliminary timeline for postmortem doc: 13:50 canary deploy start, 13:54 canary 30%, 14:00 full rollout, 14:02 errors spike, 14:10 rollback start, 14:16 rollback complete all regions, 14:20 customer comms sent.

maya (oncall): any objections to closing the live mitigation channel in 30m? If no new anomalous errors, we'll transition to RCA drafting track and tag oncall rotation for follow-up.

Jae L: no objections. I'll push the logs + list of failing request_ids into the incident artifact bucket and put link in the postmortem doc.

SRE-Bot: note: incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 14:25 after stabilization.

maya (oncall): thanks team — excellent coordination. We'll reconvene in the postmortem doc thread. If anyone finds a stray 512d host still serving prod, ping here immediately. :pray:
